fullPassage: You may have never heard of coltan, a kind of mineral found mostly in Africa. However, it contains tantalum, a rare metal that is probably a big part of your life. Tantalum is used to make tantalum capacitors, which are an essential component of cameras, laptops, and cell phones. Not surprisingly, this makes tantalum highly valuable―so valuable, in fact, that a terrible conflict is being fought over it. About 80% of the world’s coltan is found in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Currently, the country is in the middle of a violent armed conflict, and most of its coltan mines are controlled by military groups. They extract the coltan and sell it to neighboring countries, using the money to buy more weapons. More and more people are buying electronic devices containing tantalum each year. To meet this demand, large amounts of coltan must be dug out of the earth. In many cases, small children are forced to work in the mines. Many farmers, whose fields have been destroyed in the fighting, are also employed by these mines. Although they receive a fair wage, they are often robbed of their pay by armed soldiers. But humans aren’t the only ones being negatively affected. Wildlife in the area is also suffering. Endangered gorillas live in the area where coltan is mined, and they are often killed in the process of mining. The eastern region of the Congo was once home to thousands of eastern lowland gorillas; although the current population is unknown, it is believed to have been reduced by more than 50%. The conflict in the Congo is a complicated situation without an easy solution. However, businesses can improve the situation by refusing to buy any coltan coming from military groups. Moreover, within the Congo, they can work to support legitimate coltan mines, making sure the profits are used to benefit communities. Individuals can also help. By keeping our old electronic devices rather than buying new ones each year, we can reduce the demand for coltan. Then when we do upgrade to a newer model, we can recycle the old one or give it to charity instead of throwing it in the trash. Even the smallest efforts, when made by millions of consumers, can make a difference.

빈칸 앞 'a complicated situation without an easy(쉬운 ~이 없는 복잡한 상황)'가 단서예요.

① solution: 해결책 — 쉬운 '해결책'이 없는 복잡한 상황이라는 흐름 ←정답

② question: 질문 — 문맥과 안 맞아요

③ journey: 여정 — 문제 해결 문맥과 무관해요

④ custom: 관습 — 어울리지 않아요
det.tip: complicated situation without an easy ______ → 해결책(solution).

questions.passage: You may have never heard of coltan, a kind of mineral found mostly in Africa. However, it contains tantalum, a rare metal that is probably a big part of your life. Tantalum is used to make tantalum capacitors, which are an essential component of cameras, laptops, and cell phones. Not surprisingly, this makes tantalum highly valuable―so valuable, in fact, that a <u>terrible</u> conflict is being fought over it. About 80% of the world’s coltan is found in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Currently, the country is in the middle of a violent armed conflict, and most of its coltan mines are controlled by military groups. They extract the coltan and sell it to neighboring countries, using the money to buy more weapons. More and more people are buying electronic devices containing tantalum each year. To meet this demand, large amounts of coltan must be dug out of the earth. In many cases, small children are forced to work in the mines. Many farmers, whose fields have been destroyed in the fighting, are also employed by these mines. Although they receive a fair wage, they are often robbed of their pay by armed soldiers. But humans aren’t the only ones being negatively affected. Wildlife in the area is also suffering. Endangered gorillas live in the area where coltan is mined, and they are often killed in the process of mining. The eastern region of the Congo was once home to thousands of eastern lowland gorillas; although the current population is unknown, it is believed to have been reduced by more than 50%. The conflict in the Congo is a complicated situation without an easy solution. However, businesses can improve the situation by refusing to buy any coltan coming from military groups. Moreover, within the Congo, they can work to support legitimate coltan mines, making sure the profits are used to benefit communities. Individuals can also help. By keeping our old electronic devices rather than buying new ones each year, we can reduce the demand for coltan. Then when we do upgrade to a newer model, we can recycle the old one or give it to charity instead of throwing it in the trash. Even the smallest efforts, when made by millions of consumers, can make a difference.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 terrible와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: terrible=끔찍한 / pleasant=기분 좋은 / minor=사소한 / awful=끔찍한 / rare=드문
det.analysis:
① pleasant: 기분 좋은 — terrible의 반대예요

② minor: 사소한 — 규모가 작다는 뜻이라 달라요

③ awful: 끔찍한 — terrible(끔찍한)의 동의어 ←정답

④ rare: 드문 — 희소성이라 의미가 달라요
det.tip: a terrible conflict = 끔찍한 분쟁 → awful.

det.korean: extract=캐내다, 추출하다 / bury=묻다 / create=만들다 / store=저장하다 / remove=꺼내다, 제거하다

questions.passage:
(A) She bought the newest <u>model</u> of the smartphone last week.

(B) The famous athlete is a role <u>model</u> for many young students.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 model의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: model: (A) (제품의) 기종, 모델 (B) 모범, 본보기
det.analysis:
① (A) 모형 (B) 기종: (A)는 최신 '기종'을 샀다는 뜻이에요

② (A) 유행 (B) 모범: (A)는 유행이 아니라 '기종'이에요

③ (A) 기종 (B) 모형: (B)는 모형이 아니라 '모범'이에요

④ (A) 기종 (B) 모범: 최신 '기종'의 스마트폰 + 많은 학생의 '모범' ←정답
det.tip: the newest model = 기종 vs role model = 모범.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a naturally occurring solid substance, such as coltan or gold, that is dug from the ground"

det.korean: liquid=액체 / mineral=광물 / plant=식물 / gas=기체
det.analysis:
① liquid: 액체 — 고체 물질이라는 정의와 반대예요

② mineral: 광물 — 코발탄이나 금처럼 땅에서 캐내는 고체 천연 물질이에요 ←정답

③ plant: 식물 — 살아있는 생물이라 달라요

④ gas: 기체 — 고체가 아니라 안 맞아요
det.tip: 땅에서 캐내는 고체 천연 물질 → 광물(mineral).

questions.passage: Tantalum is __________ (use) to make tantalum capacitors, which are an essential component of cameras, laptops, and cell phones.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: use → used: 'Tantalum is ______'는 수동태(be + p.p.)라 과거분사 used로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'Tantalum is __________ (use)'에서 be동사(is) 뒤 자리라 수동태예요.

→ 탄탈륨이 '사용되는' 대상이니 동사 use를 과거분사 used로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 used로 써요.
det.tip: is used to ~ = ~하는 데 사용되다 (수동태).

questions.passage: More and more people are buying electronic devices __________ (contain) tantalum each year. To meet this demand, large amounts of coltan must be dug out of the earth.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: contain → containing: 명사 devices를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사라 containing으로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'electronic devices __________ (contain) tantalum'에서 빈칸은 앞의 명사 devices를 꾸며요.

→ '탄탈륨을 담고 있는 기기'라는 능동의 뜻이라 현재분사(V-ing)를 써요.

→ 동사 contain을 containing으로 바꿔요.
det.tip: devices containing tantalum = 탄탈륨을 담고 있는 기기 (현재분사 수식).

det.korean: lose all meaning=모든 의미를 잃다 / cause great harm=큰 해를 끼치다 / make a difference=변화를 만들다 / stay the same=그대로 있다

빈칸 앞 'Even the smallest efforts, when made by millions of consumers, can(수백만 소비자의 작은 노력도 ~할 수 있다)'가 단서예요.

det.tip: the smallest efforts can ______ → 변화를 만들다(make a difference).
